message.content:
{
  "verdict": "revise",
  "score": 0.28,
  "reasons": [
    "Missing complete coverage of all specified standards: the artifact only partially covers CCS1/CCS2 and CHAdeMO; NACS/Tesla, GB/T, and Type 2/Type 1 sections are entirely absent.",
    "CHAdeMO section is truncated and ends mid-thought; no complete data for typical AC power, regulatory status, vehicle compatibility, or use-cases for CHAdeMO.",
    "No dedicated, per-standard sections for NACS/Tesla, GB/T, or Type 2/Type 1, which were explicitly requested.",
    "Sources appear incomplete or non-authoritative (unclear URLs, some likely non-existent pages), and there is no consolidated sources list that supports all sections.",
    "The artifact lacks the required 3 actionable implications for a fleet buyer and does not clearly present a single Markdown file as requested.",
    "Some factual statements (e.g., transition risks and regional adoption) are presented without full, verifiable sourcing within the artifact."
  ],
  "guidance": "Produce a complete, single Markdown document that covers CCS1/CCS2, CHAdeMO, NACS/Tesla, GB/T, and IEC Type 2/Type 1 as separate standard sections. For each standard, include: (1) typical AC power ranges, (2) max DC charging speeds, (3) regional adoption/regulatory status, (4) vehicle compatibility, (5) common use-cases, (6) installation and equipment cost drivers, (7) interoperability or adapter availability, (8) major manufacturers/operators supporting it, and (9) recent market/standardization trends or transition risks. List all sources with working URLs, and finish with 3 short, actionable implications for a fleet buyer (charging uptime, future-proofing, and procurement/installation considerations). Save and deliver as a single Markdown file, current to 2026, with clear headings for each standard and consistent data fields. Validate data against authoritative sources (IEEE/IEC/ISO, government regulators, major OEMs, and large charger manufacturers)."
}
